flagged.evidence: Clause (a) supplies an interval and force only “when the model is read as forced,” but clause (b) defines the equation for t∈I₀ and every motion on an interval J⊆I₀. The free case J≡0 therefore has no specified I₀, leaving the equation and motion domain undefined for that case. The later free-mode theorem’s choice of ℝ does not supply a domain convention in this definition.

The proof says “a linear map on ℝⁿ with trivial kernel is bijective,” citing [[def-invertible-matrix-and-general-linear-group]]. That dependency only defines invertibility as the existence of B with AB=Iₙ=BA; it does not prove that an injective endomorphism of ℝⁿ is surjective. The same finite-dimensional fact is also needed to define (M^{1/2})^{-1}. Rank-nullity closes this gap immediately, so it is nonfatal.
